Michael Sanft, the Las Vegas defense attorney who represented Duane “Keffe D” Davis in the murder trial over the 1996 killing of rapper Tupac Shakur, has died at the age of 55.

Sanft was found dead at his home in Las Vegas on Friday, November 6, 2026. The Clark County Office of the Coroner confirmed his death to USA TODAY. His cause of death is pending, and no further details have been released.

Sanft was the lead trial attorney at SOS Injury Lawyers and represented Davis pro bono. Davis, 63, was convicted on August 31, 2026, of first-degree murder with the use of a deadly weapon for the fatal shooting of Shakur, and was sentenced on October 13, 2026, to 40 years to life in prison. He is the first and only person ever charged in the case. His defense team filed a notice of appeal on October 30, 2026.

Shakur was fatally shot in a drive-by shooting in Las Vegas on September 7, 1996.

Sanft’s professional biography credited him with trying more than 150 cases to a jury verdict.

Sources: USA TODAY, FOX5 Las Vegas, Las Vegas Review-Journal

title: Defense Attorney Michael Sanft, Who Represented Keffe D in Tupac Murder Trial, Dies at 55
